metaDescription: Self-propelled electric mops pull themselves across the floor, compared on pad speed, battery runtime and tank size so mopping needs little effort.
expertTake: Our top pick is the ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop, because it is self-propelled with a wide handle adjustment. The eous Cordless Electric Mop is the value pick, as it is self-propelled with one-handed control and a detachable tank. Skip self-propelled spin mops if your floors collect loose crumbs and hair, since they have no suction and will need a sweep first.
introParagraphs: A self-propelled mop uses its spinning pads to drag the head across the floor, so you steer rather than push. That removes most of the arm and shoulder load of a traditional mop and makes long sessions easier on the back.
The trade is that pad speed, battery size and tank volume are all modest in this class. Choose by how much floor you clean at a time and how much effort you want to save.

products.name: ScrubWiz Cordless Electric Spin Mop with 300 ml Sprayer
products.description:
The ScrubWiz uses a self-propelled spin design, so the pads pull the mop forward and you steer with light pressure. A 300 ml tank feeds a built-in sprayer, and the telescopic handle extends from 40 to 52 inches to fit different heights. The extension range is wide enough that both short and tall users can keep an upright posture.

Self-propulsion saves the shoulder fatigue that comes with long mopping sessions, which suits older users and bad backs. A 300 ml tank is the typical size for this class and means a refill every room or two on a messy day. It is a surface scrubber without suction, so it works best after a quick sweep. Against the eous Cordless Electric Mop, which offers a dual-spin system, a detachable tank and one-handed control, the ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop stands out for a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches.

Wash and air-dry pads after use, and rinse the tank occasionally to prevent film buildup. Check that the handle lock tightens fully after adjusting height. The battery is small, so recharge after each session.
products.bestFor: Best for users who want a self-propelled mop with an adjustable handle for comfort.
cons: Tank holds only 300 ml per fill
Battery is sized for a few rooms

products.name: eous Cordless Self-Propelled Dual-Spin Mop with Detachable Tank
products.description:
The eous is a cordless spin mop with a dual-spin head that glides itself forward, so one hand on the handle is enough. A detachable water tank lets you refill at the sink without carrying the whole machine, and an on-demand spray adds water where you need it. It is aimed squarely at light, quick daily cleaning.

One-handed control is the genuine benefit here, since you can hold a pet or open a door while mopping. As with every spin mop, there is no suction, so floors should be swept first, and the battery supports a few rooms rather than a whole house. It does not match a wet-dry washer on sticky spills. Against the KACTOR Self-Propelled Mop, which offers 160 RPM pads and a quoted 30 to 50 minutes of runtime, the eous Cordless Electric Mop stands out for a dual-spin system, a detachable tank and one-handed control.

Pads need washing after each session and spares are cheap insurance. Empty the tank after use and keep the battery charged between sessions. Check the pad hook-and-loop attachment occasionally for lint buildup.
products.bestFor: Best for light daily cleaning with one-handed ease, especially for older users.
pros: Detachable tank refills at any sink
Light enough for stairs and storage
cons: No suction, so sweep before mopping
Battery size suits a few rooms
Not a deep scrubber for dried messes

products.name: KACTOR Cordless Self-Propelled Dual-Spin Electric Mop
products.description:
The KACTOR drives two pads at 160 RPM and lets them pull the mop forward, so steering takes little force. The 2000mAh pack is quoted at 30 to 50 minutes depending on mode, and a 290 ml tank feeds an on-demand spray. LED lights at the front show dust and smears before the pad reaches them.

Runtime varies with pad drag and spray use, so plan on the lower end for sticky floors and the upper end for light touch-ups. The pads spin faster than the 150 RPM class but far slower than 800 RPM scrubbers, so it is a daily-use machine, not a grout scrubber. There is no suction, so sweep first. Against the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop, which offers quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank, the KACTOR Self-Propelled Mop stands out for 160 RPM pads and a quoted 30 to 50 minutes of runtime.

Wash both pads after use and let them dry before storing. Rinse the 290 ml tank now and then, and charge after each session to avoid deep discharge. Replacement pads are the only regular expense.
products.bestFor: Best for self-propelled daily mopping with a runtime that covers most apartments.
pros: Quoted 30 to 50 minute runtime on one charge
cons: Moderate spin speed on dried grime
Runtime drops with heavy spray use

products.name: iDOO Cordless Self-Propelled Quiet Spin Mop with Sprayer
products.description:
The iDOO emphasizes quiet running, with a self-propelled spin head and a transparent detachable tank. A sprayer and LED headlight round out the basic kit. Low noise matters if you mop while someone naps or works from home.

A quiet motor usually means gentle spin speed, so expect everyday cleaning rather than aggressive scrubbing. The transparent tank makes it easy to see when to refill, and detaching it means no lifting the whole mop. It does not suction dry debris. Against the KACTOR Self-Propelled Mop, which offers 160 RPM pads and a quoted 30 to 50 minutes of runtime, the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop stands out for quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank.

Pads need washing after each use. Rinse the tank every few weeks to prevent film. Charge after use rather than letting the battery sit empty.
products.bestFor: Best for quiet daily mopping in apartments and shared homes.
pros: Quiet motor suits early or late cleaning
Headlight shows smears on the floor
cons: Gentle spin speed on dried grime

buyingCriteria.explanation: With only one reservoir the mop redeposits what it lifted, leaving the haze familiar to anyone who mops dark tile from one bucket. Separate clean and waste chambers mean the water hitting the floor has never touched it before. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop is described by a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches, and the eous Cordless Electric Mop by a dual-spin system, a detachable tank and one-handed control, so check which one actually isolates its dirty water before you assume it does.

A spray spin mop holds roughly 300 ml, enough for a room or two, where wet-dry washers run 600 to 900 ml of clean water plus a waste tank to match. Bigger tanks mean fewer refills but more weight in your hands. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop comes with a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches, whereas the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop comes with quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank. Size the tank to your biggest single session, not to your total floor area.

Sealed hardwood and laminate cope with a damp pass but not with water pooling in the joints, which makes low-flow settings and fast drying more important than scrubbing force. More water is fine on tile and sealed stone; steam should touch sealed hard floors only. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop is built around a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches, and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop around quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank. If the floor is oiled or unsealed, check with whoever made the finish before wet cleaning at all.

Long hair and pet fur wrap around brush rolls, and a wrapped roller leaves streaks and strains the motor. Scrapers, cutting blades and hair hooks are the mechanisms that fight it, and spin pads avoid the problem but cannot lift loose hair at all. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop relies on a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches, and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop on quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank. With a long-haired pet in the house, how hair comes off the roller is the first thing to check.

A roller left wet in a closed machine begins to smell within days, so the self-clean cycle decides whether a washer gets used in year two. Better cycles rinse the roller with clean water, pull the rinse into the waste tank, and some add warm water or hot air to dry the brush. Look at ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop, listed with a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches, and compare it with iDOO Cordless Spin Mop, listed with quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank. If a model has no rinse routine, plan five minutes of manual roller care after every session.

Cordless floor tools quote roughly 30 to 50 minutes in the best case, and homes above about 1,200 square feet want 35 minutes or more before a recharge. Water use, pad drag and spin speed all shorten the quoted figure. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop lists a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches, and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop lists quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank. Do not trust a headline minute count measured at the lowest water setting if your floors are sticky.

specDecoder.watchFor: Speed varies across this lineup, from the ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop with a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches to the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop with quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank.

specDecoder.meaning: Clean-tank size sets how far you can mop before a refill. Waste tanks are usually smaller, so they often fill first.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare the tank notes on the ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop (a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches) with those on the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop (quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank).

specDecoder.meaning: Quoted runtime assumes a full charge on the gentlest setting; boost mode and heavy water use cut it down. Corded models avoid the issue entirely.
specDecoder.watchFor: Plan around the shorter end of the figures for the ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop, especially on sticky floors.

specDecoder.meaning: Some docks rinse with warm water, some add hot-air drying, and some do nothing. Heat helps break down grease on the roller and slows odor.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check the self-clean notes on ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop (a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches) against iDOO Cordless Spin Mop (quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank).

specDecoder.meaning: Capacity in mAh sets energy stored, though a faster motor and more water spray drain it quicker. Two removable packs double working time.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water handling
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, we looked at tank size, how clean and dirty water are kept apart, and how much moisture is left on the floor. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop and the eous Cordless Electric Mop sit at different points on that scale (a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches versus a dual-spin system, a detachable tank and one-handed control). Near-dry results earned higher marks here, because hardwood and laminate punish standing water.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value within this lineup
howWeEvaluated.description: Each pick was weighed against its siblings here for what its tier delivers, not against every product on the market. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop are far apart in tier, and the gap must be justified by something concrete such as a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches or quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank. Features that sound good but change little in practice carried no weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the upkeep each design hands you: cleaning rollers, rinsing tanks, washing pads and swapping filters. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop with a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop with quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank impose different routines. Anything needing daily manual scrubbing of parts lost ground to a self-clean design.

howWeEvaluated.title: Floor-type fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Intended floor types mattered here: sealed hardwood and laminate through to tile, vinyl and sealed stone. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop (a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches) and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop (quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank) are not equally suited to every surface. Steam tools were limited to sealed floors.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated how each machine actually removes dirt: spinning pads, a wiping roller, steam or a flat microfiber head. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop (a 300 ml tank and a handle that extends from 40 to 52 inches) and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop (quiet self-propelled operation and a transparent detachable tank) take very different routes. We weighted a design that handles both wet and dry mess above one that only spreads water.

maintenance.task: Clean the roller or wash the pads
maintenance.why: Caked dirt and hair reduce wiping and leave streaks. A rinsed roller or washed pad also removes odor.

maintenance.task: Clear hair from the roller ends
maintenance.why: Hair wraps around the end caps and strains the motor. A quick cut with scissors restores spin.

maintenance.task: Wipe the sensors and tank seals
maintenance.why: Film from cleaner builds on seals and sensors. Use water only and a soft cloth.

maintenance.task: Rinse and empty the dirty tank
maintenance.why: Standing dirty water sours within days. Rinse the tank and leave the lid open to dry.
A clogged filter cuts airflow and makes the motor run hotter. Rinse the filter and let it dry fully before refitting.

faq.q: Can I use vinegar or any cleaner in the tank?
faq.a: Use only the maker's cleaner or plain water, because the wrong detergent foams and can damage pumps and sensors. Vinegar is also unsafe on natural stone. If you own the ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop, follow its manual for approved cleaning solutions.

faq.q: Does a higher suction number mean cleaner floors?
faq.a: Not by itself, since Pa figures have no shared test method and roller design matters more. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop describe themselves in different terms for this reason. Judge by hair handling, water recovery and self-cleaning.

faq.q: Are these mops safe on hardwood and laminate?
faq.a: Restrict it to sealed hardwood and laminate, keep the water low and dry the floor quickly. Machines that leave floors nearly dry, such as the ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop, are safer than spray-heavy designs. Consult the floor maker first, and keep puddles away from the joints.

faq.q: Why does my washer smell after a few weeks?
faq.a: A damp roller and a closed dirty tank breed odor quickly. Start the self-clean cycle where one exists, tip out the waste tank and let the roller dry. The ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop and similar machines reward a quick routine after each use.

faq.q: How long do rollers, pads and filters last?
faq.a: Rollers and pads usually need replacing every 6 to 12 months of regular use, and filters every 3 to 6 months. Hair-heavy homes wear them sooner. Spares for the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop and similar machines should be easy to source before you buy.

faq.q: How much should I expect to spend?
faq.a: Spin mops sit at the low end and wet-dry washers at the high end, with steam and flat spray mops in between. In this guide the ScrubWiz Electric Spin Mop and the iDOO Cordless Spin Mop bracket the range. Spend more only when a feature, such as a self-clean cycle, removes a chore you would otherwise skip.
